Theorem
[Asymptotic Ricci lower bound and compactness] Source: cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0034, cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0035 1. Theorem 4.8\group section-4

Let $M^n$ be a complete Riemannian manifold such that for some $p\in M^n,\, r_0>0,$ and $v>0$ we have egin{equation} ag {4.32} \operatorname {Ric}_M(x)\ge (n-1) rac{ rac14+v^2}{r^2} \end{equation} for all $r\ge r_0$. Then $M^n$ is compact and the diameter $d_p$ from $p$ satisfies egin{equation} ag {4.33} d_p<e^{\pi /v}r_0. \end{equation}

Proof

Source: cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0035 \sketch We use the field $\mathcal{F}_{\gamma |_{[0,e^{ u }/r_0]}},$ and argue by index comparison as in the standard proof of Myers’ theorem. If $\gamma |_{[0,e^{ u }/r_0]}$ is minimal, (4.31) and (4.32) lead to the conclusion that $\gamma |_{[r_0,e^{ u }/r_0]}$ contains a pair of conjugate points.

□

We now consider the case $( rac14- u ^2)/r^2$. Observe that for $ u >0$, the conditions egin{equation} u \le rac{n+1}{2(n-1)}, \qquad - rac{n}{(n-1)^2} \le rac14- u ^2, \qquad 0 \le (n-1)\left( rac12- u ight)+1 ag {4.36} \end{equation} are equivalent to one another. Also recall that if $M^n$ is not compact, a normal geodesic $\gamma :[0,\infty ) o M^n$ is called a ray if each segment of $\gamma $ is minimal. Parts (i) and (ii) of the following theorem give a lower bound on the rate of growth of the volume of a ball, which generalizes the previously mentioned result of Yau and Calabi for the case $\Ric _M\ge 0$. A novel feature of the argument, as distinct from the case $\Ric _M\ge (n-1)H$, will be the use of a family of model spaces with metric \[ dr^2 + J^2_{ u ,R}(r)g,\qquad 0\le r\le R. \] Here the metric is expressed in polar coordinates, but the origin is at $R$. For $ u < rac12$, the metric is singular at the boundary $r=0$, while for $ u > rac12$ there is a conjugate point at the boundary. For $ u = rac12$ we have the usual flat metric on a ball of radius $R$.
